key_insight: The Patient-AI Rating instrument showed promising preliminary internal consistency for evaluating patient-perceived quality of AI health conversations.
clinical_relevance: The instrument could add patients’ perspectives to AI communication evaluation, but it does not establish medical accuracy or safety.
method: Developed with patient partners and cognitive interviews.
Surveyed adults with prior personal health-related LLM use about their own AI conversations.
Evaluated 12 quality and engagement items plus a separately scored perceived-harm item.
evidence_signal: Fourteen participants supplied 46 ratings; internal consistency was high (Cronbach’s α = 0.88; 95% CI, 0.83–0.93), and mean quality was 4.43/5.
watch_item: The small, engaged convenience sample and repeated ratings limit generalizability; absence of reported harm does not establish safety.
paper_title: Development and Preliminary Evaluation of the Patient-Artificial Intelligence Rating Instrument
